_why: Owner, 2026-10-05, verbatim: "u have a habit of half completing and half wiring up and half
connecting things". check-wiring.py already refuses a def nothing reads and an action nothing
calls. Neither of those is the defect being named: a feature wired to SOME of its call sites
and not the rest passes both, because every individual file is fine and the thing that is
missing is a call that was never written.
So each chokepoint below carries a CENSUS of every place that reaches it, and every one of
those places is either covered by a named wrapper or exempt with a stated reason. A new call
site appearing undeclared fails the build, which is the only moment anybody is in a position
to notice they are wiring up half of something.

chokepoints.name: a map is generated only where the player was warned about the freeze
why: Generation carves a 300x300 map on the main thread and the window stops answering.
An unexplained freeze reads as a crash. RimroomsGenerationNotice.Announce warns first,
moves the work into a long event, and closes out when it ends -- but a long event is only
legal where nothing is waiting on a return value, so a tick cannot use it.

Gate/GateSpinUp.cs.note: The exemption here was WRONG and said so confidently: it claimed a tick. DialRememberedAddress is reached from a FloatMenuOption delegate in GateConnectionHistory, which is a click, which is exactly where a long event is legal. The exemption had been written without reading the caller -- the same half-wiring this file exists to refuse. Now announced, and the claim is checkable in the file that holds the wrapper.

Portals/NaturalFrontierService.cs.reason: STILL EXEMPT, BUT NOT FOR THE REASON FIRST WRITTEN. The original said 'a job tick', and only one of its two callers is one: RecordDiscovery is a Toil initAction, but CompRimroomsEmergence's walk-through is a FloatMenuOption delegate, which is a click. The real obstacle is the predicate, not the caller: Discover MINTS the coordinate, so there is nothing to ask ShouldAnnounce about beforehand -- and a found door may record a way OUT, which generates no map at all. Announcing a hold that never comes is the notice becoming the nuisance, which this feature is explicitly scoped against. Covering it needs a predicate for 'this door will mint a place', which is design work and not a wrapper.

Expedition/RimroomsExpeditionComponent.c.note: The second exemption that was wrong. It said the result is read by its caller -- which described the method, not the call: Dispatch is reached from a button, the result is read INSIDE the callback, and moving ShowResult(Dispatch(...)) into the notice's continuation is the shape OperationsPortalNetwork already used. A long event is legal wherever nothing outside the callback is waiting.

Scenario/SoloGroupOpening.cs.reason: Runs inside new-game setup, where there is no frame to draw a notice on and no freeze to explain -- the player has not been shown a game yet.

chokepoints.name: every connected-work adapter asks the one traversal policy
why: Invariant 1: PortalTraversalPolicy is the only traversal chokepoint. An adapter that
forgets to ask it would quietly let a pawn cross who may not -- and `in` cannot tell one
site from seven, which is why the count is declared rather than searched for.
